articles.title: Gears of War: E-Day Story Director Laid Off Just a Week Before Early Access Launch
articles.summary: Gears of War: E-Day's story director has been laid off, just one week before the game's early access launch. Earlier today, Microsoft continued its ongoing reset of the Xbox brand, resulting in 268 staff members losing their jobs across a number of studios.
body: The news comes at a pretty brutal time, as Vaca just publicly celebrated the game going gold last week, and the title will enter early access next week, five days before its global launch. It's unclear what Microsoft is planning to do with The Coalition after Gears of War: E-Day's launch, but cutting key talent doesn't inspire a lot of confidence.

This isn't the only oddly-timed layoff, either. Halo Studios' cinematic director Josh Daniels was also laid off, just one day after getting a promotion. Halo Studios' fate is a lot clearer, however. Activision is taking charge on the future of Halo, while Halo Studios is being gutted. A small team will remain on to support existing Halo games, but a new team is being built under Activision to develop the next mainline game in the franchise.

Gears of War's future hasn't been outlined much by Microsoft. When E-Day was announced years ago, it was suggested that the team would eventually return to the ongoing storyline that was left hanging at the end of Gears 5. However, it's unclear if that's still in the cards with all of the changes happening at Xbox.

Earlier today, Microsoft continued its ongoing reset of the Xbox brand, resulting in 268 staff members losing their jobs across a number of studios.

articles.title: Wolverine's Narrative Director Explains Why Logan Needed to be a Short King in the Game
articles.summary: Wolverine's narrative director, Walt Williams, opened up about why it was important to him that Logan was made to be significantly shorter than his hulking counterpart, Sabretooth, and why the emotional aspect of their relationship was essential to portray in the game.
body: Now that Marvel’s Wolverine is out in the wild and in players’ hands, the viral discourse surrounding Insomniac’s latest superhero game has taken a different turn. Scent trails and Sentinel boss fights aside, Logan’s characterization has become a new talking point, with a vocal group of online critics arguing that Insomniac made him too ‘soft' and that their version of the character isn't tapped into his rage enough.

Speaking with journalist Gene Park on the Low Power Mode podcast, the game’s narrative director, Walt Williams, chatted about Sabretooth and Wolverine’s relationship with each other and why it was necessary to dig deep into their emotions rather than present the characters as angry, alpha mutants.

articles.title: KPop Demon Hunters And Ghostbusters Come To Monopoly Go For Spooky Season
articles.summary: It is officially the fall season in the northern hemisphere, and that means that Halloween is approaching. Mobile game giant Scopely has announced how it's celebrating, and that includes crossovers with KPop Demon Hunters and Ghostbusters in the uber-popular mobile game Monopoly Go.
body: The "Monster Mash" season, as it's called, runs September 23-November 25. During the event, players can take part in themed minigames and "immersive adventures" featuring Huntr/X and the Saja Boys from KPop Demon Hunters.

Naturally, music is a big part of the crossover event, with Huntr/X's "Golden" and "How It's Done" appearing in Monopoly Go during the event. There will also be new items to buy from the Blocks Boutique shop, including themed collectibles based on the movie. The characters Rumi, Mira, and Zoey will appear as well.

As for the Ghostbusters crossover, there are Ghostbusters-themed vehicles coming to Monopoly Go, along with locations and characters that will be familiar to fans of the films. And before you even ask, yes, the Proton Blaster is in the update as well.

Beyond these licensed crossovers, Monopoly Go's Halloween event adds the Luck-O-Lanter, which players can fill with sweet treats they find on the game board. There is also a new "dice duel" feature where players can roll dice for the chance to trick or treat their opponent based on who rolls the higher number.

body: This particular Alienware 16X Aurora gaming laptop is a second generation model that was released earlier this year. The 2026 model has been upgraded with a 16" 2560x1600 240Hz OLED display (the previous generation was IPS) and the new Intel Core Ultra 9 290HX Plus CPU. articles.title: State of Decay Developer Undead Labs Responds to 'Significant' Layoffs Following Independence from Xbox
articles.summary: Update: Undead Labs Studio Head, Philip Holt, provided the following statement to IGN, confirming that the game's release won't suffer any setbacks as a result of these layoffs. "State of Decay 3 remains in active development, and these changes will not impact the game's launch," said Holt.
body: State of Decay 3 developer Undead Labs has confirmed that it underwent "significant" layoffs following its independence from Xbox.

The studio announced on LinkedIn that it is parting ways with a "significant" number of staff. This follows the developer's separation from Xbox, which comes as a part of Microsoft's big reset for the brand that was made public earlier this summer.

"Unfortunately, today we are also saying goodbye to a significant number of our colleagues," reads the studio's announcement. "It's difficult to reach this moment knowing that not everyone who helped get us here gets to make the rest of the journey with us.

"They are exceptionally talented developers who have poured years into the State of Decay franchise: solving hard problems, looking after one another, and helping shape both this game and this studio. Their work remains part of Undead Labs and part of State of Decay 3, regardless of where their careers take them next."

Xbox announced more layoffs today following even larger cuts from this summer as part of CEO Asha Sharma's "reset." Blizzard has yet to be hit by these more recent layoffs, but reporter Jason Schreier indicated earlier this month it could be next.

articles.title: WoW: Forever Aspires To Have A “Mandela Effect” On Players
articles.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is reinventing the classic version of Azeroth with all kinds of new content, and if Blizzard does its job, players won't be able to tell the difference between what's old and what's new.
body: Announced during BlizzCon 2026, Forever introduces four new zones to Azeroth: the Riverglades, Mount Hjyal, Shen'dralas, and Zephras Isle. In an interview with GameSpot, WoW: Forever senior art director Jeff Parrott and senior game designer Josh Greenfield elaborated on how Blizzard approached developing these all-new zones so that they don't feel out of place in a 22-year old game, as well as how they tried to capture how players "remember" Azeroth looking.
Parrott said the team spent a lot of time looking back at the original, "vanilla" version of WoW and trying to understand how zones were designed back in 2004 when the game first released.

"The team did a great job of just digging in there," Parrott said. "Riverglades is a great example. I think that's a full new zone that we have, and really did a great job of leaning into that Vanilla-era kind of ethos for the design, the flow in the way everything kind of moves through the zone, the quests move you through the zone. It does feel extremely of that era, of that time. So it's really just understanding what we're aiming for and staying faithful to it."
He said the goal was for Forever's new zones to feel "familiar, but new."

articles.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Is the Cure For a Terrible RPG Habit
articles.summary: For several hours, I spent my free time meandering the world map of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave like a woman crazed. No matter what the calendar said, every day was Black Friday, and I was in feverish pursuit of gifts.
body: For Act One of Fortune's Weave, each of the game's four protagonists has a twelve-chapter story. By the time you get about partway through those chapters, your renown rank — one of several factors that allows you to recruit new teammates — starts climbing higher. Suddenly, buying the love of all those aloof prospects with swanky dinners at the inn and boatloads of fish sauce feels like a very real possibility. I spent the middle chapters of Leda's route scraping by while being underleveled, because I was more focused on expanding my team rather than improving it.

articles.title: What Is Xbox Game Studios At This Point?
articles.summary: The organizational structure of Xbox has long been complex and unwieldy, and that hasn't changed after the latest wave of changes and layoffs as part of Xbox's "reset." But Microsoft's latest reshuffling of its studios and workforce does prompt the question of what the "Xbox Game Studios" brand…
body: Not included is Mojang, the Minecraft studio that Microsoft has been leaning heavily on -- that studio now reports directly to Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

Former studios under the Xbox Game Studios brand include Rare and World's Edge, the developer of Age of Empires, but both now fall under Activision Blizzard. And while it's unclear if Halo Studios as an organization is now formally an Activision Blizzard entity, it's official that Activision is indeed making the next Halo game. Meanwhile, Xbox studio Obsidian Entertainment has jumped to Bethesda, and Turn 10 has merged with Playground Games.

Technically, all of these development teams are still Xbox studios, and Xbox will continue to publish games from partners, like OD and Physint from Kojima Productions. But the state of "Xbox Game Studios" as its own publishing label is a curiosity.

It's not outside the realm of possibility that Microsoft is doing away with the branding altogether. Since mid-2025, the Xbox website has lacked any dedicated webpages or references to Xbox Game Studios. Contrast that with PlayStation Studios, which has its own page and lists 17 studios under Sony's umbrella.

articles.title: It's Officially the End of an Era For Halo
articles.summary: Halo will never be the same. On Tuesday, Xbox announced the next phase of its ongoing restructuring, with a memo from executive vice president Matt Booty citing developer Halo Studios as the first line item in a wave of 268 new job cuts.
body: This is the sort of news that, a decade ago, would have sounded like a prank. But in 2026 — where golf course moguls can be two-term presidents and Silicon Valley can actively engineer the end of humanity with no blowback whatsoever — it’s business as usual. For Xbox specifically, it’s another chapter in a decade of brand mismanagement, and a symbolic end to one of gaming’s longtime fanbase wars.

Halo, of course, has been the face of Xbox since the very beginning. Bungie’s 2001 shooter Halo: Combat Evolved was arguably the game that moved original Xbox consoles. Its successors, 2004’s Halo 2 and 2007’s Halo 3, are still considered some of the best first-person shooters ever made, as close to universally beloved as video games get. Even the spinoffs, like Halo: Reach, were extremely well-regarded.

articles.title: Vindicated: after speaking to some pro Counter-Strike players I'm sure I was right when I said 360 Hz is the sweet spot for competitive FPS
articles.summary: A few months ago I made the case that a 360 Hz refresh rate on your monitor is the sweet spot for competitive FPS before diminishing returns kick in. I had nothing but my own testing and a big bottle of 'trust me bro' back then, but I've now spoken to a couple of Counter-Strike 2 pros and I remain…
body: At Logitech's G Play event (featuring a Counter-Strike 2 tournament) in Warsaw earlier today, I spoke to Oscar Bell, AKA 'Azuwu', and Simon Boije, AKA 'yxngstxr'. Both currently play for Luminosity, a team that particularly tugs at my CS2 heart strings given it was very big circa 2016 when I was still lapping up the tailwinds of CS:GO novelty.

Regarding refresh rates, Azuwu tells me: "When I had 240 at home, I didn't even really notice 360. But now I'm 360 I can't go back down, you know, I feel it a lot. So I think 360, 400, 600 are all pretty similar... I'd say 400 is a nice spot and 600 is extra nice. But anyway, in a lot of PCs, you won't hit 600 frames."
And Yxngstxr says: "I think it's kind of a placebo, personal thing, you know? Because on most PCs you rarely get 600 fps, right?... 600 Hz with like 300 fps, it doesn't even matter."
I run CS2 on a pretty high-end rig—featuring a Ryzen 7 7800X3D and RX 9070 XT—and I can't usually hit 600 fps in CS2, even at 1280 x 960 or 1080p. Usually I'm hovering around the 500 mark.
points: A few months ago I made the case that a 360 Hz refresh rate on your monitor is the sweet spot for competitive FPS before diminishing returns kick in.

articles.title: 'The Hunt for Gisco's Treasure' walkthrough in Fire Emblem Fortune's Weave
articles.summary: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's "The Hunt for Gisco's Treasure" quest is, at a glance, the ideal quest. You can stay in Dagsion to complete it, and you get a decent bit of money and renown when you do.
body: Below, we show you how to clear "The Hunt for Gisco's Treasure" in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave.

The quest giver has a little scrap of a riddle to help guide you. "A colossus gazes upon Baal's waters. On the stone where she points, something worthy of note." Way back when you start someone's Act 1, Seteth's narration tells you the lake surrounding Dagsion is called Lake Baal, so that's the first clue. You're hunting for something overlooking the lake, which means the port in Lowtown is the best place to go.

Happily, there's just one statue in Lowtown, just east of the Vandahl Trading Company. She's pointing east-ish, but there's no item or treasure trove or anything in sight other than a wall. That's because the treasure is on the other side of the wall, along the little path that takes you down to the harbor side.

Grab it, head back to the quest giver, and you'll get your reward: a Morfis Almanac book, 5,000 gold, and 80 renown. The book is an uncommon one, so it's a very good gift for book lovers and decent for those who prefer uncommon and rare items, like Talimun and Catania.
points: Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave 's "The Hunt for Gisco's Treasure" quest is, at a glance, the ideal quest.

articles.title: Diablo 5 will 'take a somewhat different approach' to Diablo 4's monster level scaling so your character feels noticeably stronger as you progress
articles.summary: Despite its surprise announcement at BlizzCon earlier this month, Diablo 5 is a whole three years away. Blizzard's brief teaser trailer had zero gameplay in it, which means the action RPG sequel is still mostly a mystery.
body: But director Joe Shely helped paint a picture of what the real thing might look like during a recent group interview with PC Gamer.

One of the somewhat controversial aspects of the last couple Diablo games is how they handle monster difficulty. In Diablo 2, each area has a level range that determines how tough enemies will be compared to your character. Diablo 3 and Diablo 4 ditched this approach for a system that has monsters scale in difficulty as your character levels up.

In a genre all about the power fantasy of slowly becoming a demon-slaying god, this didn't go over so well with the many players who want those moments where your character feels considerably more powerful than their foes. While this still happens in the newer games, the gap between the strength of your character and the monsters is much smaller until you're decked out in high-level gear.

Level scaling seems to solve a lot of problems with maintaining a certain degree of challenge in the newer Diablo games, but it does diminish the spikes in power you can get from finding a particularly strong item or leveling up.
points: Despite its surprise announcement at BlizzCon earlier this month, Diablo 5 is a whole three years away.

articles.title: Artist who hand-paints some of gaming's best fantasy world maps brings them together in oversized and extremely lavish art book
articles.summary: If you're an enjoyer of video game maps, you might like this: celebrated artist and cartographer Francesca Baerald - who's created in-game (and out) maps for Dragon Age, Warcraft, Octopath Traveler, Diablo, Dungeons & Dragons and many more - is releasing a glossy new art book.
body: Unbound - The Cartography Art Book by Francesca Baerald, as it's known, is currently being crowdfunded. But it's already a huge success on Kickstarter, having raised more than four times its £20k goal with weeks to spare. The book includes more than 250 maps from Baerald's work in video games, tabletop RPGs, board games, and graphic novels.

If Baerald's name is familiar, it might be because I talked to her for a long piece I wrote about the creation of game maps a couple of years ago. What I found especially intriguing about her work was that Baerald creates maps almost exclusively physically, by painting in watercolour, rather than using digital software to create them.

"I believe a perfect map should inspire players and readers from the first glance," Baerald told me at the time. "I see maps not as instruments to find directions in a game, but as decorated, welcoming doorways that drag you into the game's world."

videos.summary: Thanks to Nvidia for sponsoring the video. To learn more about how Nvidia tech delivers the best possible fidelity and performance in games like Control Resonant, click the link:
body: Control Resonant adopts the structure and aesthetic of a Ubisoft style open world game full of map markers and regional bosses, but whereas in a Ubisoft game the structure is the experience, here the structure is the beginning of a process that is specifically designed to subvert expectations. Rather than dictate the game's ultimate form, the structure is simply a scaffold that exists to let Remedy build other, more interesting things.
